title: The Cultural Programme and the Gift of Kaḷiru
paragraphs: > The male of the elephant is kaḷiṟu. > Kaḷiṟu denoting the male pig > Is not disallowed too.
> Kalai is the male of the deer too; > Kalai is also the male of the langur (mucu).
Narrated below is a humorous incident by which to remember kaḷiṟu, kēḻal, kalai and mucu used in the verses.

The king returns home after victory in a war. The soldiers are indulging in fun and frolic. The court jesters are singing the victory song and dancing with the soldiers inebriated with toddy. After some time, they stop singing and one of the
court jesters says to his counterpart, “Sir, Court Jester, you can make use of your good offices to arrange a cultural programme by beautiful damsels.”
“Not a big deal at all. I will arrange it, right now.”

The other court jester replies and leaves the place. He returns then parading a black langur by holding the rope tied to its neck. The jester thrusts a stick into monkey’s hand and gestures it to dance. The soldiers burst into peals of laughter, whereas the other court jester enquires in rage, “What is this, sir? Is this a beautiful woman? Do you call this a cultural programme?”
The court jester who has arranged the monkey dance replies,

“As per the rules prescribed in Tolkāppiyam, kalai means mucu. Kindly refer to the dictionary, where you will find the meaning of mucu to be a black langur. Leave that alone. I promptly arranged the cultural programme heeding to your request . Now, why don’t you give me a reward?”
“Recommend to the king, I may be given a kaḷiṟu (male elephant) as a reward.”
Why recommendation to the king? I will myself give you a kaḷiṟu as a reward. Please wait a moment, here, I will come.”
He reappears after some time, dragging a male pig along with him.

“Dear jester, here is the kaḷiṟu which you asked for as a reward. In the very same Tolkāppiyam which you cited as a reference, a male pig, along with a male elephant, is referred to as a kaḷiṟu. Here, do accept your beautiful kaḷiṟu,” he says.

This triggers an infectious roar of laughter among the soldiers. The cultural programme and the reward of kaḷiṟu have made them laugh to such an extent that their ribs have started aching. It turns out to be a perfect revelry on victory in the war.
The meaning of the verses is:
1. The male elephant is known as kaḷiṟu. The male pig is also known as kaḷiṟu. 2. Kalai is the apt word for deer, Which designates mucu the black langur too.
